ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 4 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — Srinivasa Ramanujan

code.originalText: Six weeks: recovery, final sputum cultures, liver tests before rifampin, vitamin B12, mood, influenza vaccine

text.paragraph: Six weeks: recovery, final sputum cultures, liver tests before rifampin, vitamin B12, mood, influenza vaccine. [S]

Mr. Ramanujan returns six weeks after diagnosis. He finished paromomycin as planned and his stools returned to normal within two days. He has had no fever, the pain under his ribs has gone, and he has gained almost 3 kg. He is cooking twice a day now, with milk and curd daily, and takes his vitamin B12 and weekly vitamin D. He sees the counselor weekly, calls his family each Sunday, and has been to two community meals with families from the local Tamil association. The final sputum cultures from January show no growth at six weeks; Dr. Raghunathan reviewed them and the plan for latent infection by message. He is working full days again. [S]

tr.td: Evening fevers to 38.6 °C with night sweats for about four weeks
S — Synthetic presenting symptom, superseded by the diagnosis at the second visit.
Weight loss of 5 kg over two months (57 to 52 kg), with poor appetite
S — Synthetic presenting symptom, superseded by the diagnosis at the second visit.
Dull right upper quadrant pain for three weeks, worse on deep breathing and lying on the right side, with a tender liver edge
S — Synthetic presenting symptom, superseded by the diagnosis at the second visit.

Amebic liver abscess: a single 6.2 x 5.4 cm abscess in the right lobe (segment VII) on ultrasound, Entamoeba histolytica antibody positive, blood cultures negative, years after two episodes of dysentery in India; treated with metronidazole and then paromomycin; synthetic modern diagnosis linked to the hepatic amoebiasis later proposed for his illness
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis; it does not settle the historical diagnostic conflict (CLM-0010, CLM-0011).
Vitamin B12 deficiency from a strict vegetarian diet (B12 168 pg/mL), with anemia (hemoglobin 11.2 g/dL, MCV 99 fL) to which inflammation also contributes
S — Synthetic finding anchored to his documented diet and the vitamin deficiency later proposed.
S — Synthetic finding anchored to his documented diet and the vitamin deficiency later proposed.
Positive interferon-gamma release assay, with chest radiograph and sputum smears and NAAT negative for tuberculosis; cultures pending
S — Synthetic finding, superseded by the diagnosis of latent infection when cultures were negative.
Latent tuberculosis infection: positive interferon-gamma release assay, normal lungs on the radiograph, three sputum smears, NAAT and cultures negative; treated with four months of rifampin
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis; active tuberculosis was excluded, which does not settle the historical question.
Adjustment disorder with depressed mood (PHQ-9 12, no thoughts of self-harm) during a serious illness, far from his wife and family
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis anchored to his documented loneliness; not a claim about his real mental health.

list.item:
Amebic liver abscess (A06.4). Clinically resolved after metronidazole and paromomycin: CRP 6 mg/L; alkaline phosphatase 118, ALT 28, AST 24 U/L, bilirubin 0.6 mg/dL, albumin 3.9 g/dL. [S]
No repeat imaging while he stays well.
Three-month review.

Latent tuberculosis infection (Z22.7). Cultures negative at six weeks with negative smears, NAAT and radiograph: active tuberculosis excluded. The positive IGRA is latent infection, worth treating at his age and after recent illness. With normal liver tests and the abscess treated, rifampin for four months is the preferred, shortest daily regimen; it does not interact with his vitamins, though it speeds vitamin D breakdown. [S]
Rifampin 600 mg each morning before breakfast for 4 months.
Orange urine, sweat and tears are expected; stop and call for jaundice, rash, or vomiting.
Monthly clinical checks and liver tests at two months.

Vitamin B12 deficiency with anemia (D51.3). Hemoglobin 12.6 g/dL from 11.2, MCV 94 fL; B12 410 pg/mL. Responding. [S]
Continue B12 daily, long term.

Adjustment disorder with depressed mood (F43.21). PHQ-9 8 and GAD-7 6. Safety reviewed: no thoughts of suicide or self-harm; safety plan current. [S]
Continue weekly counseling and weekly calls home.

Follow-up: Monthly clinical check on rifampin; preventive visit in about six weeks. Three-month review with blood count, liver tests, vitamins and mood. Call for jaundice, rash, vomiting, or fever. Next scheduled visit 2026-04-06: periodic adult preventive visit with pre-travel advice. [S]
